context:
Goal: a hidden failure never slips past you, and the guard never cries wolf.
Problem (rule): rule git-never-discard-output (keep command output) says every command, but its guard checks only git writes, so the rule and its check disagree.
Based on (read): CLAUDE.md rule git-never-discard-output: "Keep command output. Discarded output hides failures from the reader."
Based on (read): hooks/guard.py, refusal silent-write, reads only git writes silenced by a null redirect or -q; `npm test >/dev/null 2>&1` passes (docs/plans/refusal-vs-rule.md:46).
Based on (read): rule tokens-run-through-verdict already keeps test output in a log through `verdict`.
Departs from: main, a rule wider than its guard — makes the rule and the guard say the same thing.

options.gain: The rule says exactly what is enforced; no false alarms on ordinary /dev/null use.
options.how: Rewrite the rule text: never silence a git write's output. Test runs stay covered by the verdict rule.
options.label: Narrow the rule to git writes
options.lose: A non-git command silenced to /dev/null is no longer against any rule.

options.gain: Every silenced command is caught, as the rule text says now.
options.how: Extend silent-write to refuse any command whose output goes to /dev/null.
options.label: Widen the guard to every command
options.lose: Many ordinary reads that discard noise get refused; the guard starts to cry wolf.

ref: deep audit 1102, report docs/plans/deep-audit/report.md on audit/deep-1102 (6b6a41f3), table 'claude-settings: homes', row output-discard-rule-scope
title: Should the keep-output rule cover only git writes, as the guard does, or should the guard grow to all commands?
why: The verdict wrapper already covers test runs; a wider guard would refuse routine /dev/null use.
